title: What If Antibiotics Stopped Working?

scenes.text: What if antibiotics stopped working? It has already started.
Drug-resistant bacteria directly caused about 1.14 million deaths in 2021, according to a study in The Lancet.
It's been at least a million deaths every year since 1990, and more than thirty-six million in total.
The Lancet forecasts nearly two million deaths a year by 2050, and thirty-nine million between 2025 and 2050.
Older people are hit hardest. Deaths among people seventy and over rose by more than eighty percent.
It's the quiet version of this what-if, happening slowly, one resistant infection at a time.
